svg.text: A. The tunnel: wn-server serve with relay = true (v1)
Owner's browser
outside the home
The edge
wn-cloud, relay-edge, holds the TLS cert
wn-server
relay package + reverse proxy, at home
wn-cloud API
v2 web service + Postgres
Navidrome
child process, Unix socket only
1 GET /servers/:id with the server credential
→ relay.connect_url, relay.host, addresses; stored, reused when wn-cloud is unreachable
2 TLS to connect.relay.waxnerd.com:443, then GET /v1/tunnel
Bearer <server credential>, Upgrade: wn-relay/1, Wn-Server-Id: <server id>
3 token check as for any CLI token; the token's user owns the server id;
relay_enabled and relay_until on servers (7-day grace). Else 401, 402 relay_not_enabled, 403, 409.
4 101 Switching Protocols, Wn-Relay-Host: <id>.relay.waxnerd.com
both sides start yamux; the edge opens streams, wn-server serves them with http.Server
5 keepalive ping every 30 s; last_seen_at written every 60 s;
credential and entitlement re-checked every 10 min; a drop reconnects with backoff and jitter
6 servers.relay_connected_at, relay_last_seen_at, relay_streams; relay_usage per month
Result: one outbound connection from the home, authenticated once with the credential wn-server already holds. A second tunnel for the same server replaces the first.
wn-server status shows: connected since <time> at https://<id>.relay.waxnerd.com. The LAN path is unchanged; a failure of the tunnel never stops serve.
B. The owner opens the web UI from outside the home (v1). The edge checks nothing per request.
Owner's browser
outside the home
The edge
TLS ends here
wn-server
relay package + reverse proxy
wn-cloud API
not called per request
Navidrome
Unix socket
1 GET https://<id>.relay.waxnerd.com/ui/
wildcard certificate; routed by host; caps checked (in-flight, audio, egress, body, per-IP rate)
2 same request on a yamux stream, header X-Relay-Client: <client IP>
no session, no password, no account is checked here
3 relay package: moves X-Relay-Client into the context, marks the request relayed,
hands it to the proxy handler in process; r.TLS != nil || relayed is the TLS-terminated test
4 sign-in form: account name + app password → Set-Cookie wn_session; Secure; Path=/ui/
Origin checked against r.Host = the relay host; limiter keyed by the forwarded client address
5 /rest/* on the socket with Remote-User, X-Forwarded-Host: <id>.relay.waxnerd.com,
X-Forwarded-Proto: https; share links therefore carry the relay host
6 response passes back unchanged; the edge counts bytes and audio responses per tunnel
Authentication is wn-server's. A third-party Subsonic client uses the same address with the app password. POST /api/v1/session answers 403 not_available through the relay in v1.
wn-server's router is the allowlist: /rest/*, /share/*, /api/v1/*, /, /ui/*. The edge refuses Upgrade (400), other methods (405), bodies over 1 MiB (413), and a host with no tunnel (502).
C. A listener signs in from a first-party client (after v1, designed, not built)
Listener's client
first-party app, outside the home
The edge
forwards, checks nothing
wn-server
checks membership itself
wn-cloud API
members, invites, device codes
Navidrome
one non-admin user per listener
1 the owner invited the listener and the listener accepted at wn-cloud (listener row in server_members, cap 12)
the client signs in with the listener's waxnerd account, reads the server's addresses, and gets a device code bound to the server
2 POST /api/v1/session with the code at the relay host; the edge forwards it down the tunnel
3 POST /servers/:id/device-codes/verify → user_id, role
accepted only when the cached member list (refreshed every 5 min) holds the user
4 first sign-in: listener account in wn-server + non-admin Navidrome user (native API)
5 wn-server session for the listener; every later request is checked locally and forwarded with Remote-User
The owner is never refused. A listener is served from the cached member list for 30 days of wn-cloud outage, then refused until a refresh succeeds (WAX-945, decision 2).
The web UI stays owner-only. A listener's ratings stay local until first-party clients write them to wn-cloud with the listener's own account.
